Course 04

Personality without labels

Traits, differences and assessment.

Lesson 2. The Big Five

1 · Lesson

The most studied trait model is the Big Five. It arose from analysing the words languages use to describe people and from studying questionnaires in many countries. Its dimensions are:

  • Openness to experience: curiosity, imagination, liking for novelty.
  • Conscientiousness: organisation, persistence, self-discipline.
  • Extraversion: sociability, energy, seeking stimulation.
  • Agreeableness: cooperation, trust, consideration for others.
  • Neuroticism (or emotional instability): a tendency to experience negative emotions easily.

These dimensions predict, on average and modestly, things like academic and job performance (conscientiousness), well-being (neuroticism and extraversion) or relationship quality (agreeableness). No score is "better" in itself: each pole has advantages and drawbacks depending on the context.

2 · Example

A high neuroticism score is often seen as negative, but it is also associated with greater sensitivity to risks. A very high agreeableness score makes living together easier but can make it harder to set boundaries. Traits describe tendencies, not virtues or flaws.

3 · Activity

Without taking any test, place yourself from 1 to 10 on each of the five dimensions. Ask someone who knows you well to do the same about you. Where do you agree and where not? Why do you think that is?
